items.summaryText:
When you hear that data is the new oil, this is ultimately what that looks like. AI has such a thirst for data that we’re entering an era where it’s valuable almost in any form.

In a world of AI, information actually belongs as an asset on the balance sheet. This data sale is just one example of the implications of what that will look like.

Ultimately, the way that companies manage and mine their organization’s intelligence will be one of the deciding factors for competitiveness and value creation in the future.

当你说数据是新的石油时，最终呈现出来的就是这个样子。AI 对数据的渴望如此之大，以至于我们正在进入一个几乎所有形式的数据都有价值的时代。

在 AI 的世界里，信息实际上应该作为资产负债表上的一项资产。这次数据出售只是这种趋势影响的一个例证。

归根结底，公司管理和挖掘其组织智能的方式，将成为未来竞争力和价值创造的决定性因素之一。

items.title: The best way to get good at evals is to  take a workflow you know really well an…
items.summaryText:
The best way to get good at evals is to  take a workflow you know really well and figure out how to make its quality measurable.

Study the actual traces - the sequence of prompts typical users have, what good responses would look like at each step and for the end to end outcome. 

Study where your product fails and create traces that capture them - messy tool call responses, missing context etc.

Once you have a good eval, think about how you would make it easy to run repeatedly and automatically. 

Once you have that, think about how you will ensure your eval continues to mirror live traffic as your users patterns evolve.

This could be a series. Would you guys like me to write about it everyday?

metadata.bio: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.

items.summaryZh:
擅长评估的最佳方法，是找一个你非常熟悉的工作流程，然后想办法让它的质量变得可衡量。

研究实际轨迹——典型用户的一系列提示词、每一步以及端到端结果中好的回答应该是什么样子。

研究你的产品会在哪里失败，并创建能捕获这些失败场景的轨迹——混乱的工具调用响应、缺失上下文等等。

一旦你有了一个好的评估，想怎么让它能轻松地重复和自动运行。

有了之后，再想怎么确保随着用户模式演变，你的评估能持续反映真实流量。

这可能可以做成一个系列。你们想让我每天都写吗？

items.title: My hottest take is that brand marketing is going to be THE major differentiator…
items.summaryText:
My hottest take is that brand marketing is going to be THE major differentiator and one of the most prized assets for a company going forward. 

And, I’m not talking about launch videos or pouring money primarily for “aesthetics” simply to pump the valuation. You still need retention before attention. 

I’m talking about thinking through what a company stands for and understanding the “vibe” of what’s happening in the market. Being relentless on the long term goal while also thinking through how to showcase the company in the short term. And doing it every week. 

Especially if you think agents become the primary user for most products, then to get the attention of a rapidly attention deficit audience (aka humans) you’ll need to stand out consistently in how you present the company. 

These folks primary have been given tier 2 roles and passed up for CMOs many many times. I think this will finally invert in the next 10 years where you’ll hire these folks as cofounders or at least give them a big seat at the table. 

Normally the design centric CEO tends to be this, but those are rare and you’ll need to learn how to hire for this role. Just like a good product marketer, these are exceptionally rare so you have one hold them close!!

metadata.bio: partner @fpvventures - investing in seed/A. previous: early hire @meter, @opendoor, @atlassian & others. love @shimoleejhaveri + 👦👧

items.summaryZh:
我最强烈的观点是，品牌营销将成为未来公司的关键差异化因素，也是最宝贵的资产之一。

而且，我指的不是发布视频，也不是单纯为了推高估值而主要把钱投在“美学”上。在获得关注之前，你仍然需要留存。

我指的是想清楚一家公司代表什么，理解市场正在发生的“氛围”。对长期目标保持执着，同时思考如何在短期内展示公司。而且每周都要这样做。

特别是如果你认为代理（agent）会成为大多数产品的主要使用者，那么要吸引一群注意力严重缺失的受众（也就是人类），你需要在展示公司的方式上持续脱颖而出。

这些人过去大多只能担任二线角色，多次在 CMO 的选拔中被忽略。我认为这将在未来 10 年内最终逆转：你会把这些人招为联合创始人，或者至少给他们一个重要的席位。

通常以设计为中心的 CEO 会扮演这个角色，但这样的人很少，你需要学会如何为这个角色招聘。就像优秀的品牌营销人员一样，这种人极其罕见，所以如果你拥有一个，一定要紧紧抓住他们！！

items.bodyText:
Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:11
70% of France is still nuclear in terms of its power generation. 70%. Where are all the accidents and where are all the kerfuffles and, you know, nothing. Nothing's happened. US is 18%, and we haven't built a reactor in forty years.

Speaker 1 | 00:11 - 00:25
We had a safety lobby in the seventies basically kill abundant clean energy for us. There are real outcomes where safety has hurt us. And the question is where do we want the spectrum to be on AI for this stuff? And there's many worlds, many scenarios, many outcomes.

Speaker 2 | 00:31 - 01:03
Hi, listeners. Welcome back to No Fires. Today is just me and Alad talking about risk management, RSI, how many trillion dollar companies there can really be, and the ills of regulatory capture. For any new founders out there, it's also time to apply to embed Conviction's low overhead, high signal grant program for 10 exceptional startups building at the frontier. We hold this program twice a year, and it's $250,000 in cash on an uncapped note, well as compute and services from our partners, OpenAI, Anthropic, Base10, and others.

Speaker 2 | 01:04 - 01:24
Most importantly, it's about the company you keep. Our first handful of cohorts have included companies like Cognition, Chai Discovery, Listen Labs, Physical Intelligence, and Flappy Airplanes, people advancing the frontier and diffusing AI into every corner of the economy. Find the app online at embed.conviction.com. Okay. Let's get started.

Speaker 1 | 01:24 - 01:26
Sarah G. How are doing? You

Speaker 2 | 01:27 - 01:31
A lot. It's good to see you. It's been a while since we just get to hang out with each other.

Speaker 1 | 01:32 - 01:34
I know. It's been too long. What happened? Where you been?

Speaker 2 | 01:34 - 01:38
You know, working at companies in DC, trying to take a day off. You?

Speaker 1 | 01:39 - 01:44
There's just so much going on right now in AI. There's so much going on. It's nonstop. It's very exciting times.

Speaker 2 | 01:44 - 01:48
You're chasing chasing the next trillion dollar company?

Speaker 1 | 01:48 - 02:03
Yeah. It's a it's a really interesting point because basically what we had is over the last five years or so, we had three companies roughly go from close to zero to a trillion dollars in market cap. Right? Anthropic basically didn't exist five years ago. OpenAI was still quite early.

Speaker 1 | 02:03 - 02:22
I think GPT-three just come out, and SpaceX was trading at 80, a 100, something like that. And so suddenly, we had this massive inflection in terms of valuations of these companies. And I think a lot of people now are assuming that there's a bunch of other trillion dollar companies that will be formed in three to five years. And that's unprecedented in human history. Usually, it takes twenty years.

Speaker 1 | 02:22 - 02:40
SpaceX actually took since the early 2000s, and Google took since the nineties. These are usually fifteen, twenty year arcs. And then we had this weird five year inflection. And so I feel like a lot of people now are looking at different areas that are very exciting, very promising areas, robotics, materials.
